svg.title: What is Node.js?
svg.desc: Auto-playing 48s step-by-step explainer of "What is Node.js?" (from img.png + img_1.png). Each step is highlighted in turn with what happens, why it matters, missing concepts added in lime, and a Node.js code example. Hover to pause.
svg.text: Node.js is a JavaScript runtime built on Google's open-source V8 JavaScript engine. What that sentence really means.

g.text: What: Node.js = V8 (runs the JavaScript) + libuv (async I/O) + Node APIs (fs, http,
crypto...). Together they let JavaScript run outside the browser.
Why: This one definition explains everything later in the course: the event loop, the thread
Added: Each step unpacks one part of the definition, plus things the slide does not mention
(REPL, JIT, browser vs Node, npm, LTS).
What: You write ordinary JavaScript in a .js file and run it from the terminal with "node
app.js". No HTML page, no browser tab.
Why: JavaScript escapes the browser: the same language can now read files, open ports and
Added: Type "node" with no file to open the REPL, a live JS console for trying snippets (the
globals list in img_3 comes from there).
What: V8 is the engine that actually executes your JavaScript. Node embeds the very same V8
Why: V8 only knows the JavaScript language itself (objects, functions, promises). It has no
idea what a file or a network socket is.
Added: V8 starts by interpreting bytecode, then JIT-compiles "hot" functions to fast machine
code, and frees unused memory with a garbage collector.
// NOT from V8 (these come from Node):
What: Node wraps V8 with extra APIs written in C++ and JS: file system, networking, crypto,
OS info, plus libuv for asynchronous I/O.
Why: Engine + these APIs = a "runtime". That is exactly what "JavaScript runtime built on
Added: Browser and Node share the language but not the APIs: Node has no document / window /
DOM; the browser has no fs or process.
What: The node binary runs on every major OS, so the same app runs on your laptop, a VPS, a
Docker container or a serverless function.
Why: One language for frontend, backend, tooling (Vite, ESLint) and even desktop apps
Added: npm ships with Node to install packages. Use LTS versions (even numbers: 20, 22) in
What: Node.js is not a language and not a framework: it is a runtime. JavaScript is the
language; Express is a framework that runs on Node.
Added: REPL, JIT + garbage collector inside V8, browser vs Node APIs, npm, and LTS versions.
A: A JavaScript runtime: Google's V8 engine
so JS can run on servers, not just browsers.

svg.text: Language comes from V8, I/O powers from Node
Calling Node a language or a framework
Using window / document in Node code
A: Your JS runs on 1 thread; libuv uses more
